To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cosmological model with the T-M and the L_x-T scaling relations is consistent only with low density universes, and that the T-M and especially the L_x-T relations can be constrained with galaxy cluster data.

1) the cosmological parameters Omega and Lambda can be constrained with galaxy cluster data; 2) only low density universse (Omega approx.0.3 with and without Lambda) are consistent with the current data; 3) the T-M and the L_x-T scaling relations can be constrained with the same data; 4) the T-M relation is consistent with the current X-ray data, and the L_x- T relation is consistent with both X-ray and SZ data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of galaxy clusters, and the constraints that can be placed on cosmology using the cluster data.
the study of galaxy clusters, which are the largest objects in the universe.
the following questions: What is the nature of the dark matter in the universe?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the framework of the cosmological model we used, the data are consistent with low density universes, and with the T-M and the L_x-T relations.
the data sets used in this work are compatible with low density universes and that they are not compatible with high density universes (with Omega greater than 1).
the data are consistent with the cosmological model and the cluster scaling relations, but the data are not yet conclusive enough to make strong statements about the model or the relations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cosmological parameters are not very well constrained by galaxy cluster data.
the combination of X-ray and SZ data can give a very strong constraint on Omega and Omega_M, which will be further improved with future data.
we can get information about the scaling relations using cluster data and that the scaling relations are consistent with each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of cluster data with other data sets can be very powerful to constrain cosmological parameters.
we have shown how the joint fit to the cluster model and to the T-M and the Lx-T relations is a very powerful tool to get cosmological constraints and to study the cluster scaling relations.
the cosmological model and the scaling relations are strongly correlated, and therefore it is not possible to fit them separately.
